newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rails against social evils, crime.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rails against social evils, crime.

text.p: Vietnam's Communist Party called on Tuesday for a blitz on social evils, crime and traffic chaos to ensure order and security during next month's lunar new year festival, Tet.
"Social evils such as drunkenness, gambling, drug abuse, and social disorder...easily mushroom during the traditional Tet holiday," the party newspaper Nhan Dan said in an editorial.

"Ensuring safety for everyone to enjoy Tet is the policy of the party and state," it said. "Party cells and authorities at all levels are responsible for directing police forces to spearhead the maintenance of security and order."
Although Tet is traditionally a time of feasting and family celebration, it has in recent years become an occasion for the country's youth to let off steam.
New Year firecrackers have now been banned and the authorities have moved to blunt the exuberance of urban youth by closing down illegal bars and clamping down on illegal motorbike races.
Nhan Dan reeled off a list of statistics to illustrate that crime rings, smuggling, theft and armed robbery were on the increase.
It also bemoaned the rising death toll on the country's roads. The number of traffic accidents rose by 22 percent in 1996 to about 20,000, in which nearly 6,000 people were killed and 21,000 injured.
